prompt: A note-taking app must suggest tags on a phone with no internet connection.
tells: on a phone with no internet connection
why: Small language models like Phi can run on a device.
trap: A large cloud model can't run offline on a phone.

prompt: You need to sort 2 million support emails a day into 5 simple categories as cheaply as possible.
why: A simple task at huge volume suits a small, cheap, fast model.
trap: A reasoning model would work but cost far more for no gain.

prompt: An autocomplete feature must respond in under 100 milliseconds while the user types.
trap: Provisioned throughput steadies latency, but a large model is still slower than a small one.

prompt: A factory wants a model running on a cheap local box to answer simple questions about machine logs, with no data sent to the cloud.
tells: running on a cheap local box
no data sent to the cloud
why: Local, low-cost hardware points to a small language model.
trap: Data-zone deployment keeps data in a region, but still in the cloud.

prompt: A team uses a reasoning model to translate short product titles and complains it is slow and expensive.
why: Simple tasks don't need a reasoning model; a small, fast model fits better.
trap: The fix is a different model choice, not a bigger limit or reserved capacity.

prompt: A team wants a cheap model they can fine-tune on 5,000 examples to label support tickets, running on modest hardware.
why: Small language models are cheap to fine-tune and run.
trap: Labeling tickets doesn't need deep reasoning.

prompt: A clinic wants a chat helper that runs entirely on its own laptops so patient notes never leave the building.
tells: runs entirely on its own laptops
why: Only a small model can run on a laptop.
trap: A data-zone deployment still sends data to the cloud.
